title: It's time
description: This article in a series explores how the unknown can be known without prediction, by acting coherently inside irreversible time. It argues that time is order, not a dimension to traverse, and that events cannot be undone—only reinterpreted through new action. Using examples from physics, history, and personal experience, it shows that agency arises from the coupling of reason (what is structurally possible) and conscience (whether action is still possible). Knowing, in this view, is not revelation but the costly alignment of phases across systems, where coherence reduces energy and allows small actions to shift large trajectories. The text also includes a proof of the Collatz Conjecture.
